patch_description: Instead of routing every partition of every destination independently along the same shortest path (which piles num_partitions × N flows onto one route and overloads its throughput constraint), this approach treats the broadcast as a group routing problem. It computes k-shortest diverse paths per destination, then assigns partitions across those paths to balance load — like a multi-commodity fanout. It also builds a shared Steiner-tree-inspired "trunk" so destinations with overlapping routes reuse edges, reducing redundant transfers. Edge costs are weighted by cost/available_throughput to prefer cheap, uncongested links, and load across parallel edges is spread so per-edge flow stays below throughput.
